headline: Tech rout extends into Friday as AI-cost fears sink Asia, Nasdaq futures slide while PCE in-line gives the dollar a mild overnight fade.
stance: The week's defining story is a painful unwind of crowded AI and semiconductor positions: the Nasdaq is on pace for a 4.4% weekly loss even as the broader S&P 500 holds better and the Dow outperforms — classic rotation out of mega-cap tech into defensives and industrials. Thursday's PCE inflation print came in broadly in line with expectations, which nudged the dollar and Treasury yields slightly lower overnight and gave gold a modest bounce off the cash-close low, but the Fed's hawkish posture under Chair Warsh is unchanged — markets still price roughly a 63% chance of a September rate hike. The path of least resistance pre-open is lower for tech, steadier for everything else.

news.head: PCE in line, Fed stance unchanged
news.body: May PCE inflation matched forecasts, easing the very worst fears of a hot surprise, but it leaves the Fed's hawkish bias intact with markets pricing ~63% odds of a September rate hike.

news.head: Global AI sell-off deepens
news.body: A broad rotation out of AI and semiconductor stocks accelerated overnight: Asia's tech-heavy indices collapsed, with South Korea's KOSPI triggering circuit-breakers and closing down roughly 10%, as SK Hynix and Samsung each fell ~12%.

news.head: Nasdaq four-day losing streak
news.body: The Nasdaq Composite has now logged four consecutive down sessions — its longest losing streak since February — and is on pace to close the week roughly 4.4% lower.

news.head: Qualcomm AI revenue outlook
news.body: Qualcomm's upbeat long-term AI revenue forecast offered a rare counter-narrative in an otherwise risk-off tape for semiconductors, providing a partial sentiment floor.

news.head: IBM sub-1nm chip breakthrough
news.body: IBM announced a sub-1nm chip technology breakthrough, though shares slipped on the news, suggesting investors are focused on near-term valuation risk rather than long-dated product catalysts.

news.head: UMich sentiment due today
news.body: The final University of Michigan June consumer sentiment reading is due this morning — a soft print could add to the risk-off mood; a resilient number could provide a modest floor.

news.head: Oil retreats to pre-conflict levels
news.body: Crude oil has now fully retraced its war-premium as US-Iran peace negotiations progress, with WTI trading near $70.84 overnight (OVERNIGHT LEVEL) — reducing inflation pressure but crimping energy equity upside.

implications: The simultaneous drop in tech and oil removes two previous inflation arguments, which is marginally friendly for bonds — 10Y yields edged down to ~4.37% overnight (OVERNIGHT LEVEL) from the prior cash close of 4.40%.

A fifth consecutive down session in Nasdaq futures would confirm that the AI-valuation de-rating is broader than a single-day shock; watch whether dip buyers emerge at the open or capitulation accelerates.
Dollar softness overnight (DXY ~101.13, OVERNIGHT LEVEL, vs. prior cash close of 101.44) is modest — the macro driver of hawkish Fed expectations remains dominant, capping any sustained DXY selloff.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in S&P 500 futures (10th percentile of 3 years), Nasdaq 100 futures (9th percentile), and Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile — a 3-year low) — a contrarian floor that argues against chasing the sell-off aggressively. Separately, speculators are piled into copper longs (97th percentile) — a contrarian warning for industrial metals despite copper's extreme 95th-percentile price level.

Primary dealers are warehousing near-record high-yield bond inventory (97th percentile of 3 years), meaning their balance sheets have less room to absorb client selling — a latent credit fragility to monitor if equities keep falling.

watch.head: UMich sentiment (9:30 ET)
watch.body: Final June reading — consensus expects a weak number; a surprise to the upside could stabilize tech sentiment.

watch.head: Nasdaq open print
watch.body: Whether NQ futures recover from the overnight -0.66% (OVERNIGHT LEVEL) at the open or accelerate lower is the single biggest tell for today's tape.

watch.head: USD/JPY at 161.776
watch.body: The yen is at its most extreme level in 3 years (100th percentile); any sharp yen strengthening — a sign of carry-trade unwinding — would amplify equity vol and signal broader risk-off.

watch.head: Gold $4,024 overnight
watch.body: Gold futures are at an OVERNIGHT LEVEL of ~$4,024 vs. prior cash close of $4,044.50 — holding above $4,000 is a key sentiment test; a break below risks accelerating precious-metal liquidation.

watch.head: WTI crude $70.84 overnight
watch.body: Oil at an OVERNIGHT LEVEL of ~$70.84 continues to fall on easing Middle East tensions; watch whether a break below $70 inverts the narrative for energy equities.

watch.head: 10Y yield 4.37% overnight
watch.body: Treasuries have caught a small safe-haven bid overnight; a move back above 4.40% (prior cash close) would signal that inflation fear is reasserting itself.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10Y Treasury yield: prior cash close 4.40%; overnight level ~4.37% — a small safe-haven bid as equities weakened in Asia.
2Y Treasury yield: prior cash close 4.09%, giving a yield curve of +31 bps (prior cash close) — still historically flat, meaning the market sees rate cuts eventually but not soon.
Real (inflation-adjusted) 10Y yield stands at 2.19% (prior cash close) — that is genuinely restrictive and is the primary headwind for high-multiple tech stocks.
10Y inflation breakeven: 2.21% (prior cash close) — markets believe inflation will stay above the Fed's 2% target, keeping the pressure on Chair Warsh to hold or hike.
DXY dollar index: prior cash close 101.44; overnight level ~101.13 — slight softening after in-line PCE, but the dollar's multi-week rally is intact given hawkish Fed pricing.
Bond market volatility (MOVE index): 67.1 (prior cash close) — relatively contained, meaning the rates market is not in panic mode despite the equity sell-off.

Financial conditions remain loose overall: the Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index sits at -0.477 (as of Jun 19) and the St. Louis Fed Stress Index at -0.96 — these are pre-stress readings, not danger signals.
Weekly jobless claims: 215K (as of Jun 20) and the 4-week average at 224K — labor market still firm, which removes the urgency for the Fed to pivot.
sections.positioning: Speculators are washed out of 3M SOFR interest-rate futures (1st percentile of 3 years — a 3-year low in bullish bets) — a contrarian-bullish lean for short-term rates, suggesting the market may be pricing in too many hikes.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500: prior cash close 7,357.49; futures OVERNIGHT LEVEL ~7,307 (-0.69%) — the broad index is holding better than tech.
Nasdaq 100: prior cash close 25,358.60; futures OVERNIGHT LEVEL indicating further pressure (-0.66%) — fourth consecutive losing session.
Dow Jones: prior cash close 51,920.62; Dow futures OVERNIGHT LEVEL ~51,821 (-0.19%) — outperforming as rotation continues into industrials and financials.

VIX fear gauge: prior cash close 18.89 — elevated but not at panic levels; the Nasdaq VXN (tech-specific fear gauge) is notably higher at 30.91 (prior cash close), confirming the sell-off is concentrated in tech.
SKEW index at 139.9 (prior cash close) — options traders are paying up for downside protection, a sign of lingering tail-risk anxiety.
Market breadth is mixed: 62.1% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day average (prior cash close), but only 48.5% of Nasdaq 100 stocks do — confirming the tech-specific nature of the weakness.
The equity-credit correlation stands at 0.774 (prior cash close) — stocks and credit are moving very closely together, so any stress in one market quickly bleeds into the other.
CAPE (Shiller P/E): 41 (prior cash close) — still stretched at historically high valuations, which is why AI-valuation anxiety triggers outsized moves.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in S&P 500 (10th percentile), Nasdaq 100 (9th percentile), Russell 2000 (2nd percentile — a 3-year low), and VIX (14th percentile) futures — across the board, speculators are washed out, which is a contrarian floor and argues against panic-selling here.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — at the epicenter of the global AI-chip sell-off, yet large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) and a burst of unusual options buying appeared on Jun 25; company insiders have been buying; shorts are light (2.61 days to cover) limiting squeeze risk; trades above its 200-day average. Signal is fresh — monitors as a potential mean-reversion long if Asia stabilizes.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield vs. investment-grade spread: 276 bps (as of Jun 24) — the gap between riskier and safer corporate bonds is contained; no credit panic despite equity volatility.
Investment-grade bond spread (OAS): 75 bps (prior cash close) — tight, consistent with still-easy financial conditions.
Commercial paper funding spread: 21 bps (as of Jun 19) — short-term corporate borrowing costs are normal; no funding stress.
Bank reserves: $2,951 billion (as of Jun 24) — ample system liquidity; the plumbing is not under pressure.
Overnight reverse repo (RRP) facility usage: $5.7 billion (prior cash close) — near zero, confirming excess cash has largely drained out of this safety valve; money is in the system.
Treasury General Account (TGA): $918.7 billion (as of Jun 24) — a large government cash balance; future spending drawdowns would inject liquidity into markets.
M2 money supply growing at 5.58% year-over-year (as of May) — moderate monetary backdrop, neither deflationary nor inflationary extreme.
Loan syndication rate at 6.94% (as of Jun 24) and bank credit growing 6.38% year-over-year — lending channels remain open.

single_name.note: NewtekOne (NEWT) — small-business lender; 2 insider buying signals fired, large off-exchange block buying, a burst of unusual options activity, trades above 200-day average; shorts are heavy at 18.24 days to cover, creating meaningful squeeze risk if credit sentiment stays stable. Signal is fresh.
